questions.question: Distribution in the hospitality industry refers to

options.A: the cooking methods used in the kitchen.
options.C: the channels customers buy through.
options.D: the number of floors in a hotel.

questions.explanation: The channels customers buy through. Distribution includes how services reach customers, such as a hotel's website, travel agents, and online travel agencies. Cooking methods, uniforms, and building size are not distribution.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature and scope of distribution

questions.question: Last month, a hotel's average guest satisfaction score was 4.6 out of 5, but scores ranged from 1 to 5. What should a manager conclude?

options.A: Most are satisfied, but some low scores need review
options.C: The scores are meaningless because they vary
options.D: Every guest gave the hotel a score of exactly 4.6

questions.explanation: Most are satisfied, but some low scores need review. A high average shows overall satisfaction, but the wide range means some guests were very unhappy, which deserves attention. An average doesn't mean everyone gave that score, low scores show some dissatisfaction, and variation is useful information.

performanceIndicator.text: Interpret descriptive statistics for business decision making

questions.question: Delphine wants to compare the number of guests at four resort restaurants last month. Which visual would make the comparison clearest?

options.C: A bar graph comparing the four

questions.explanation: A bar graph comparing the four. Bar graphs make it easy to compare amounts across categories at a glance. A paragraph is harder to compare quickly, a map shows locations rather than amounts, and photos don't display numbers.

performanceIndicator.text: Display hospitality and tourism data in charts/graphs or in tables

questions.question: The renovation of a hotel's lobby is two weeks behind because a flooring shipment is late. Which is the best corrective action?

options.A: Tell the crew to stop all work until the flooring arrives
options.B: Rearrange the schedule so other tasks are completed while waiting
options.C: Open the lobby with no floor
options.D: Install a cheaper floor without approval

questions.explanation: Rearrange the schedule so other tasks are completed while waiting. Rearranging tasks keeps the project moving and limits the delay. Stopping all work wastes time, changing materials without approval may violate the plan, and opening an unfinished lobby would be unsafe and unprofessional.

performanceIndicator.text: Monitor projects and take corrective actions

questions.question: Why might a new travel agency use secondary information before conducting its own research?

options.A: It is always more current than primary information
options.B: It is designed specifically for the agency's questions
options.C: It is never available to competitors
options.D: It is usually faster and less expensive to obtain

questions.explanation: It is usually faster and less expensive to obtain. Secondary data, such as industry reports, is often free or inexpensive and available immediately. However, it may be outdated, wasn't collected for the agency's specific needs, and competitors can access it too.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain sources of secondary hospitality and tourism information

questions.question: Which piece of information is essential to record when a guest calls to order room service?

options.C: The guest's employer

questions.explanation: The guest's room number. The room number tells staff where to deliver the order and which account to charge. A favorite color, home address, and employer aren't needed to complete a room service order.

performanceIndicator.text: Process telephone orders in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: A small tour company invites travel bloggers on a free trip so they will write about the experience. This promotional method is designed to generate

options.C: personal selling.

questions.explanation: Publicity. Publicity is unpaid media attention. By hosting bloggers, the company hopes they'll share positive stories with their readers. Sales promotions are short-term incentives like coupons, personal selling is one-on-one selling, and direct mail sends messages to customers' mailboxes.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain promotional methods used by the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Which of the following is the best way to determine a guest's needs:

options.A: Ask open-ended questions and listen carefully
options.B: Talk mostly about the business's services
options.C: Rely only on the guest's appearance
options.D: Assume all guests want the same things

questions.explanation: Ask open-ended questions and listen carefully. Open-ended questions, such as "What brings you to town?", encourage guests to share details, and careful listening reveals what they want. Assumptions, one-sided sales talk, and judging by appearance often miss real needs.

performanceIndicator.text: Determine hospitality and tourism customer/guest needs

questions.question: A hotel offers a manager's complimentary dessert to a couple whose dinner was delayed. When processing this comp, the server should

options.A: record it under the comp policy.
options.B: tell the couple it's a coupon.
options.C: charge the couple for it quietly.
options.D: skip recording it to save time.

questions.explanation: Record it under the comp policy. Complimentary items must be recorded so managers can track costs and inventory, even though the guest isn't charged. Charging the guests would be dishonest, calling it a coupon is inaccurate, and skipping the record creates accounting problems.

performanceIndicator.text: Process complimentary offers and coupons/discounts

questions.question: A caller claiming to be a guest's spouse asks the front desk for the guest's room number. According to standard security policy, the clerk should

options.B: describe the guest's schedule for the day.
options.C: offer to connect the call to the room.

questions.explanation: Offer to connect the call to the room. Hotels protect guest privacy by never giving out room numbers. Offering to transfer the call lets the guest decide whether to talk. Sharing the number or schedule risks the guest's safety, and hanging up is rude when a safe alternative exists.

performanceIndicator.text: Follow established security procedures/policies

questions.question: A hotel recorded room service orders over five nights: 12, 15, 15, 18, and 20. What is the median number of orders?
questions.explanation: 15. The median is the middle value when data are listed in order. In 12, 15, 15, 18, 20, the middle value is 15. The mean is 16 (80 / 5), 18 is the fourth value, and 20 is the highest value.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the use of descriptive statistics in business decision making

questions.question: Why do many hotels avoid saying a guest's room number out loud at the front desk?

options.A: Room numbers are confidential to housekeeping only
options.B: Guests prefer to guess their room number
options.C: Others nearby could overhear it and enter the room
options.D: It takes too long to say the number

questions.explanation: Others nearby could overhear it and enter the room. Announcing a room number allows anyone nearby to learn where a guest is staying, creating a safety and theft risk. Instead, clerks write it down or point to it on the key packet. The practice is about guest security, not speed or housekeeping.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain security considerations in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: A luxury hotel provides 24-hour butler service, while a budget motel offers self-serve breakfast and basic housekeeping. What best explains the difference in their service practices?

options.A: Their target guests expect different levels of service
options.B: Budget motels are not allowed to offer more services
options.C: Butlers are required by law in all hotels

questions.explanation: Their target guests expect different levels of service. Each business designs service around the expectations and willingness to pay of its target market. Budget motels choose simpler service to keep prices low. Neither type is barred from offering services, luxury hotels do compete, and butlers aren't legally required.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify factors affecting customer-service practices in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: Communicating a hospitality company's core values to customers helps the company

options.C: reduce the number of employees.

questions.explanation: Build trust in its brand. When customers understand what a company stands for, such as sustainability or warm service, and see it in action, they trust the brand and know what to expect. Communicating values doesn't replace advertising, justify raising every price, or reduce staffing needs.

performanceIndicator.text: Communicate core values of product/service

questions.question: Which of the following should a letter of application do:

options.A: Repeat the résumé word for word
options.C: Include the applicant's salary demands in the first sentence
options.D: Explain the applicant's interest and qualifications

questions.explanation: Explain the applicant's interest and qualifications. A letter of application introduces the applicant, connects his or her skills to the job, and requests an interview. Repeating the résumé adds nothing new, opening with salary demands seems presumptuous, and the letter should be about one page.

performanceIndicator.text: Write a letter of application

questions.question: Which of the following is a factor that motivates many travelers to choose a vacation destination:

options.A: The color of the destination's welcome signs
options.B: The number of parking spaces at the airport
options.C: Unique attractions they can't find at home
options.D: The size of the local government

questions.explanation: Unique attractions they can't find at home. People often choose destinations for experiences they can't get elsewhere, such as natural wonders, culture, or famous attractions. Airport parking, sign colors, and government size rarely drive destination choice.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain factors that motivate people to choose a hospitality and tourism site

questions.question: When planning evacuations, why must a hotel consider guests with mobility challenges?

options.A: They can use elevators during fires
options.B: They are not allowed to stay above the first floor
options.C: They should evacuate last
options.D: They may need extra assistance or designated safe areas

questions.explanation: They may need extra assistance or designated safe areas. Guests who use wheelchairs or have other mobility challenges may need help or a protected area of rescue until responders arrive. They can stay on any floor, shouldn't be left behind, and elevators generally shouldn't be used during fires.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify factors affecting evacuation procedures/protocols

questions.question: Consumer spending is an important economic indicator because it

options.A: shows how much money banks print.
options.B: is the same as the unemployment rate.
options.C: is a large share of economic activity.

questions.explanation: Is a large share of economic activity. Household spending on goods and services accounts for the majority of economic activity in the U.S., so changes in it signal whether the economy is growing or slowing. It doesn't measure government purchases, unemployment, or money printing.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the measure of consumer spending as an economic indicator

questions.question: Why is it difficult for a hotel to make up for an empty room on a slow night?

options.A: Hotels can store unused rooms for busy seasons
options.B: Hotel rooms are perishable and can't be sold later
options.C: Rooms can be shipped to other hotels
options.D: Guests always pay for rooms they don't use

questions.explanation: Hotel rooms are perishable and can't be sold later. Hospitality services are perishable. If a room goes unsold tonight, that night's revenue is lost forever. Rooms can't be saved for later or moved elsewhere, and guests do not pay for rooms they never booked.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of product in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Two days after guests check out of the Alpine Lodge, they receive a thank-you email with a link to a gallery where they can download photos taken during their ski lessons and share them online. The lodge is using digital media to

options.C: train its housekeeping staff on new tasks.

questions.explanation: Enhance the post-sales experience. After the stay, a personal email invites guests to relive and share the experience, strengthening loyalty and word-of-mouth. Rate setting, check-in, and staff training happen through other processes.

performanceIndicator.text: Use digital media to enhance customer post-sales experience

questions.question: A hotel's front desk team includes employees from four generations who prefer different ways of communicating. What is the best way for the manager to handle this?

options.B: Assign work based on age alone
options.C: Use several methods and set clear expectations
options.D: Require everyone to communicate only by text message

questions.explanation: Use several methods and set clear expectations. Using a mix of methods, such as meetings, emails, and messaging, while setting clear standards helps everyone stay informed. Forcing one method excludes some employees, assigning work by age is discriminatory, and ignoring differences can lead to misunderstandings.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss issues associated with workplace diversity (e.g., ethnic, generational, religious, gender)

questions.question: A guest asks for a room close to the elevator because of a mobility issue. Which of the following should the front desk clerk do:

options.A: Ask the guest to prove the mobility issue
options.B: Make every reasonable effort to meet the request
options.C: Tell the guest that requests aren't allowed
options.D: Assign the guest the farthest room available

questions.explanation: Make every reasonable effort to meet the request. Accommodating special needs shows respect and care, and may be required by accessibility laws. Refusing requests, ignoring them, or asking for proof of a condition would be poor service and could be discriminatory.

performanceIndicator.text: Accommodate special needs/specific requests of customers

questions.question: Thunder Ridge, a theme park known for its roller coasters, builds a water park next to its existing rides and begins selling a combined ticket for both. Thunder Ridge is creating a

options.C: price war.

questions.explanation: Product extension. A product extension adds new offerings related to an existing product, helping the business reach new customers or encourage longer visits. A recall removes unsafe products, a price war involves competitors cutting prices, and market withdrawal means leaving a market.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of product extensions in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Which of the following is information a hotel can obtain from its customer database:

options.B: How often a guest has stayed in the past
options.C: The guest's exam scores in school
options.D: What the guest ate at a competitor's restaurant

questions.explanation: How often a guest has stayed in the past. A hotel's database contains its own records, such as stay history, preferences, and spending. It doesn't hold information from competitors, and it shouldn't contain private medical or school information.

performanceIndicator.text: Obtain business information from customer databases

questions.question: A supply chain is

options.A: a type of metal used in construction.
options.B: a list of a company's employees and suppliers.
options.C: a group of stores owned by one company.
options.D: the businesses that make and deliver a product.

questions.explanation: The businesses that make and deliver a product. A supply chain links suppliers of raw materials, producers, distributors, and retailers to get products to consumers. It isn't a construction material, a retail chain, or a staff list.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of supply chain

questions.question: A guest tells the concierge she has one free afternoon and loves art but dislikes crowds. Which recommendation best meets her needs?

options.B: A weekday tour of a small gallery
options.C: A full-day bus tour of the region

questions.explanation: A weekday tour of a small gallery. The gallery tour matches her interest in art, avoids crowds, and fits her time. An amusement park is crowded and unrelated to art, a sold-out evening concert isn't available or timely, and a full-day tour is longer than her free afternoon.

performanceIndicator.text: Recommend hospitality and tourism services

questions.question: A hotel's managers disagree about whether to renovate the pool or the fitness center first. Which action would best help them build consensus?

options.C: Let the loudest manager make the final call
options.D: Discuss each option and find common goals

questions.explanation: Discuss each option and find common goals. Talking through the benefits and focusing on shared goals, such as guest satisfaction, helps the group reach an agreement everyone can support. Letting one person dominate, leaving it to chance, or avoiding a decision doesn't build consensus.

performanceIndicator.text: Use consensus-building skills

questions.question: A guest checks in for an anniversary stay. Which suggestion by the front desk clerk is the best example of up-selling?

options.A: Telling the guest the hotel is fully booked
options.B: Suggesting the guest look for a room at a competitor
options.C: Offering a suite upgrade with a view for a small fee

questions.explanation: Offering a suite upgrade with a view for a small fee. An upgrade to a special room fits the occasion, increases the guest's enjoyment, and raises revenue. Saying the hotel is full or sending the guest elsewhere loses business, and a smaller room is the opposite of up-selling.

performanceIndicator.text: Up-sell to enhance customer experience

questions.question: An event coordinator wants a reminder before each client meeting. Which feature should she use?

options.C: Spell check

questions.explanation: Calendar alerts. Calendar alerts notify users before scheduled events, helping them stay on time. Spell check corrects writing, formulas calculate numbers, and screen savers protect displays.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate personal information management/productivity applications

questions.question: Why do hospitality businesses use data mining?

options.A: To avoid collecting any guest information
options.B: To find trends that improve service and sales
options.C: To prevent employees from using computers

questions.explanation: To find trends that improve service and sales. Data mining turns large amounts of booking and sales data into insights, such as popular packages or likely repeat guests, that guide marketing and service. It is not used to delete data, restrict computer use, or avoid collecting information.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of data mining

questions.question: Web analytics tools help a hospitality business

options.C: cook menu items faster in the kitchen.

questions.explanation: Track website visitor behavior. Analytics tools report website traffic, pages viewed, time spent, and where visitors came from, which helps improve online marketing and bookings. They don't schedule staff, affect cooking, or make keys.

performanceIndicator.text: Use analytical tracking tools

questions.question: Jada loves organizing details, working with vendors, and seeing large gatherings come together. Which hospitality career best matches her interests?

options.C: Event planner

questions.explanation: Event planner. Event planners coordinate venues, vendors, schedules, and guests for weddings, conferences, and other gatherings. Night auditors balance hotel accounts, line cooks prepare food, and lifeguards supervise swimmers.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain career opportunities in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: Isabella is writing a report recommending whether her hotel should add an airport shuttle. Which content is most important to include?

options.A: A description of her favorite vacation
options.C: Jokes to keep readers interested
options.D: Data on guest demand and estimated costs

questions.explanation: Data on guest demand and estimated costs. Decision makers need evidence about demand and costs to judge whether the shuttle is worthwhile. Personal stories, unrelated photos, and jokes don't support the recommendation.

performanceIndicator.text: Prepare written reports for hospitality and tourism decision-making

questions.question: When selling a gift certificate, an employee should record the amount and a unique number to

options.C: limit who can receive it.
options.D: raise the price of the certificate.

questions.explanation: Track redemption and prevent fraud. Recording each certificate's value and number lets the business verify it when it's used and prevents copies from being redeemed. Recording doesn't change the price, restrict recipients, or replace giving a receipt.

performanceIndicator.text: Sell gift certificates in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: A couple calls a travel agency to plan a trip but isn't sure where they want to go. Which question will best help the agent learn their needs?

options.C: "Do you want the most expensive package?"
options.D: "What do you enjoy doing on vacation?"

questions.explanation: "What do you enjoy doing on vacation?" An open-ended question about activities gives the agent information to match destinations to the couple's interests. Pushing the most expensive option, sending them away, or suggesting one place without understanding their interests doesn't identify needs.

performanceIndicator.text: Determine hospitality and tourism customer/guest needs

questions.question: A tour company sees that bookings rise each year when a nearby city hosts a large festival. Which conclusion is best supported by this information?

options.B: Bookings are unrelated to local events
options.C: The company should stop offering tours that week

questions.explanation: The festival brings more customers. The repeated link between the festival and bookings supports the conclusion that festival visitors are booking tours. The data shows the opposite of reduced interest, suggests bookings are related to events, and gives no reason to cancel tours.

performanceIndicator.text: Draw conclusions based on information analysis

questions.question: Why should kitchen employees keep garbage containers covered and away from food-prep areas?

options.A: To avoid emptying the trash each day
options.B: To save money on cleaning supplies
options.C: To make the trash easier to fill

questions.explanation: To prevent pests and contamination. Open garbage attracts insects and rodents and can spread bacteria to food and surfaces, which risks foodborne illness. Covering trash and keeping it away from prep areas is a basic sanitation practice, not a way to avoid emptying it or save on supplies.

performanceIndicator.text: Practice safe and sanitary handling/disposal of wastes/recyclables

questions.question: Why should a cashier compare the signature or ID of a customer paying by credit card when the business's policy requires it?

options.C: To record the customer's birthday

questions.explanation: To help prevent fraudulent purchases. Verifying identity helps confirm the person using the card is the cardholder, which reduces fraud losses. It doesn't make the transaction faster, it isn't used to collect birthdays, and sales tax is calculated by the register.

performanceIndicator.text: Process sales transactions (e.g., cash, credit, check)

questions.question: Which of the following is a career in the food and beverage segment of the hospitality industry:

options.C: Airline pilot

questions.explanation: Executive chef. Executive chefs lead restaurant and hotel kitchens, planning menus and managing staff, which places them in food and beverage. Pilots work in transportation, travel insurance agents in travel services, and housekeepers in lodging.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain career opportunities in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: A quality culture is one in which

options.A: every employee takes responsibility for quality.
options.B: customers are responsible for finding mistakes.
options.C: quality is checked once a year.

questions.explanation: Every employee takes responsibility for quality. In a quality culture, all employees are committed to meeting standards and improving processes in their daily work. Leaving quality to managers, checking it rarely, or relying on customers to find problems are signs of a weak quality culture.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe crucial elements of a quality culture

questions.question: A restaurant chain shares its weekly sales forecasts with its produce supplier so the supplier can plan harvests and deliveries. What is the main benefit of this collaboration?

options.C: Fresher products with less waste

questions.explanation: Fresher products with less waste. When the supplier knows what's needed, it can deliver the right amounts at the right time, improving freshness and reducing spoilage for both companies. Sharing forecasts usually lowers costs, doesn't limit menus, and speeds rather than slows deliveries.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the benefits of supply chain collaboration

questions.question: A theme park groups its visitors into clusters based on the rides, food, and shows they choose. This technique helps the park

options.C: clean the park overnight.
options.D: set the height of its roller coasters.

questions.explanation: Identify groups with similar interests. Clustering groups customers with similar behavior, helping the park target promotions and design packages for each group. It doesn't affect ride design, payroll, or cleaning.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate basic data mining techniques

questions.question: Online review sites have changed the hospitality industry mainly because

options.A: they prevent businesses from responding to reviews.
options.B: guests share experiences that influence others.
options.C: they guarantee every business good ratings.
options.D: they replace the need for customer service.

questions.explanation: Guests share experiences that influence others. Reviews give travelers peer opinions before they book, which pushes businesses to maintain quality and respond to feedback. Businesses can respond to reviews, ratings are not guaranteed to be positive, and good service is still essential.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain ways that technology impacts the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: While explaining room options, a hotel clerk notices that the guest keeps looking at her watch and tapping her foot. The clerk should

options.C: ask about her vacation plans.

questions.explanation: Get to the point quickly. Looking at a watch and tapping a foot suggest impatience, so the clerk should respect the guest's time and get to the point. Slowing down, chatting, or walking away ignore the cues and could frustrate the guest further.

performanceIndicator.text: Interpret others' nonverbal cues

questions.question: After booking a group's hotel stay, a sales manager calls the group leader a week before arrival to confirm details and answer questions. This follow-up helps

options.C: build a lasting client relationship.

questions.explanation: Build a lasting client relationship. Following up shows care and helps prevent problems, making the client more likely to book again. It isn't meant to cancel the booking, affect taxes, or avoid providing the services.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the role of customer service as a component of selling relationships

questions.question: Guests at Lakeview Resort often mention in reviews that staff remembered their names and preferences. This shows that positive experiences are strongly linked to

options.C: low prices.

questions.explanation: Personalized service. Remembering names and preferences makes guests feel recognized and valued, showing the power of personalized service. Low prices, technology, and building size may matter to some guests, but they aren't what these reviews describe.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify factors associated with positive customer experiences

questions.question: Which of the following should an effective leader do when leading change:

options.B: Explain why the change is needed
options.C: Punish employees who ask questions
options.D: Make changes as secretly as possible

questions.explanation: Explain why the change is needed. People are more likely to support change when they understand the reasons and how it affects them. Announcing without explanation, punishing questions, and secrecy increase resistance and fear.

performanceIndicator.text: Lead change

questions.question: A family arrives at a hotel late at night after a delayed flight. Which action by the night clerk creates a positive moment of truth?

options.A: Reciting every hotel policy before handing over keys
options.B: Asking them to wait while she finishes a personal call
options.C: Greeting them warmly and checking them in quickly
options.D: Telling them their room might not be ready

questions.explanation: Greeting them warmly and checking them in quickly. A warm greeting and quick check-in turn a stressful arrival into a positive impression. Personal calls, uncertainty about the room, and long policy explanations would make the tired family's experience worse.

performanceIndicator.text: Deliver positive moments of truth

questions.question: A tour company wants detailed opinions from eight frequent customers about possible new trips. Which method is best?

options.C: A billboard

questions.explanation: A focus group. A focus group allows a small group to discuss ideas in depth and react to each other's opinions. Billboards are advertising, receipts record transactions, and a census collects population data rather than opinions about tours.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe methods used to collect hospitality and tourism business information (e.g., observations, mail, telephone, Internet, discussion groups, interviews)

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of unstructured business data:

options.C: A table of nightly room rates

questions.explanation: Comments in online reviews. Unstructured data doesn't fit neatly into rows and columns. Examples include written reviews, emails, photos, and videos. Room rates, hours worked, and dates are structured data that can be organized in tables.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify challenges with the use of unstructured business data
